surface_verification.justification: Backend-only Python CLI entry point (release.py) mechanising FR-01.08 AC02/AC05; no client/** UI, API route, SSE/WS handler, or message contract is touched -- nothing for a browser/API surface runner to drive. Verified with 177 in-process pytest tests plus 4 real-subprocess E2E CLI tests (test_release_e2e_cli.py) exercising the module across a process boundary.

behaviors.behavior: AC02: a release is refused before any host contact when tests are failing and unconfirmed
AC02: a release proceeds once a person confirms despite failing tests
AC02: no test-results file at all refuses (unconfirmed) and proceeds once confirmed
AC02: a corrupt/unparseable results file and a non-object JSON root are both treated as failing, not silently as no-results
AC02: the gate recognises both the top-level and iterate_latest-nested shipwright_test_results.json shapes
a deploy (host) failure mid-release is reported with its own failure_stage, never raised or conflated with a smoke failure
PROD stays ASK-FIRST: an unrecognised --target and a PROD target without --confirm-prod both refuse before any host contact; PROD proceeds once confirmed
AC05: a successful smoke check never triggers a rollback

AC05: a failed smoke check with a configured polling deadline automatically rolls back to the previously-live ref, recorded invocation=auto in the audit trail, and the restored ref is re-verified healthy (or reported unhealthy) by a post-rollback recheck
AC05: auto-rollback is skipped (not fired) when no polling deadline was configured -- a single fixed-timeout attempt is not trusted to trigger a host mutation
AC05: auto-rollback is skipped, with a named reason, when there is no distinct previous ref (new environment) or the deployed ref matches the previous one
AC05: a lock-timeout writing the rollback audit trail never crashes an auto-rollback that already mutated the host -- it degrades to the durable marker
an invalid --smoke-poll-interval (discovered only once smoke verification is reached, after deploy) degrades to a structured smoke_config failure, never an uncaught traceback
the CLI's argv-to-release() wiring maps refused/released/not_released outcomes to the documented exit codes, and a --profile load error is reported before any release attempt

release.py works end to end as a real subprocess across a process boundary: refusal, confirmed deploy, auto-rollback, and skip-smoke-when-no-url paths, with the hosting token never leaked to stdout/stderr
the shared hosting.hosting_errors() classification degrades gracefully when the jelastic_client module does not define JelasticError, and includes it when present
